title: SpecInfer: Accelerating Generative Large Language Model Serving with Tree-based Speculative Inference and Verification
technique: tree-based speculative inference: multiple small SSMs build a token tree, LLM verifies the whole tree in one pass with tree attention; multi-step speculative sampling

optimized_metrics.evidence: This paper introduces SpecInfer, a system that improves the end-to-end latency and computational efficiency of LLM serving with tree-based speculative inference and verification.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: we let all systems generate up to 128 new tokens and report the average per-token latency in Figure 7. (§6.2)

optimized_metrics.evidence: To preserve an LLM's generative performance, SpecInfer must guarantee that its tree-based speculative inference and verification mechanism generates the next token by following the exact same probability distribution as incremental decoding.

headline_claim.text: SpecInfer outperforms existing LLM serving systems by 1.5-2.8x for distributed LLM inference and by 2.6-3.5x for offloading-based LLM inference, while preserving the same generative performance.

reported_metrics.where: Table 1-3, Fig 9 (verified tokens per decoding step; success rate)

metric_definitions.term_as_written: average per-token latency / end-to-end inference latency
metric_definitions.definition_quote: For each prompt, we let all systems generate up to 128 new tokens and report the average per-token latency in Figure 7.
metric_definitions.notes: Latency per generated token averaged over a 128-token generation; SpecInfer may produce more than 128 tokens. Request batch size (concurrent requests) 1-16 on x-axis; not serving under arrival process.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we focus on the average number of tokens that can be verified in each stochastic decoding step
metric_definitions.notes: Table 2 greedy, Table 3 stochastic; success rate of verifying a token in Table 1.

load_regime: fixed batch size (1-16 concurrent requests), 128 new tokens per prompt, offline
tradeoff_acknowledged: Improvement over incremental decoding shrinks as batch size grows (less spare GPU compute); larger tree width increases verification latency at large batch (BS>=4)
hardware: 1 or 4 A10 GPUs (tensor parallel), 2 nodes x 4 A100 (65B); single 24GB GPU for offloading
models: LLaMA-7B, OPT-13B, OPT-30B, LLaMA-65B; LLaMA-68M/OPT-125M SSMs
extractor_notes: 'End-to-end latency' in text is operationalized as average per-token latency; comparison vs vLLM/TGI/FasterTransformer/FlexGen. No tail percentiles, no SLOs. Abstract says 'end-to-end latency' but figures plot per-token latency.
